newsitem.title: FRANCE: Truckers lift Bordeaux fuel depot barricade.
newsitem.headline: Truckers lift Bordeaux fuel depot barricade.

text.p: Striking truckers lifted their last barricade outside fuel depots in southwest France on Tuesday after a union member was crushed to death by a lorry he was trying to stop, unions said.

The unions voted to continue their strike despite lifting the barricades set up on Monday as part of a campaign to put pressure on bosses to keep promises of early retirement and higher pay after a 12-day strike last year.

Judicial sources said truck driver Jacques Hellebois, 40, was likely to be placed under formal investigation for manslaughter on Tuesday after his truck crushed unionist Didier Pinson at a roadblock outside the Ambes fuel depot on Monday.
The unions lifted the blockade outside the Ambes fuel depot after the killing. On Tuesday, they lifted their other roadblock, at the Ambares depot.

A prosecutor said Pinson, of the Force Ouvriere union, died after he slipped off the running board and under the truck after exchanging blows with Hellebois through the cab window, trying to make the truck stop.
Union members would lay a wreath later on Tuesday in the Ambes industrial zone in memory of Pinson.
The death overshadowed Monday's day of action by the truckers.

They say employers have failed to honour a pact last year granting retirement at 55 instead of 60 for drivers with 25 years' service, sick pay, travel expenses, union rights and a ban on Sunday driving. They also agreed a special bonus payment of 3,000 francs ($600).
Talks about implementing the deal broke down when unions and haulage bosses failed to meet a March 31 deadline.
